chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Umeyra, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the drowned person: is he washed? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he is absolved (of minor impurities).' I said: 'And how is he absolved?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is left for three days before he is buried; and similarly, the one struck by lightning, for perhaps they think he has died and he has not died.'

key_terms.يُسْتَبْرَأُ: He is absolved (cleansed of minor impurity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ritual ruling for washing and burying the drowned or those struck by lightning in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi addresses the juridical uncertainty surrounding sudden deaths like drowning or lightning strikes, where death might not be immediately apparent. It establishes a practical protocol of leaving the body for three days to confirm death before burial, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on verifying life status to ensure the validity of ritual washing (ghusl) and burial rites.
